You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

{"scenario":"Merlin Textile workshop","question":"Can a customer representative confirm compliance for lot K19?","claims":{"A":"The workshop bought lot K19 in February.","B":"Lot K19 met its minimum wash-fastness rating on receipt.","C":"Lot K19 was ordered as red silk."},"handoff":"The case concerns whether a customer representative can confirm compliance for lot K19 from Merlin Textile workshop. Claim A, that lot K19 was purchased in February, is well supported by a signed purchase record (S1). Claim C, that the lot was ordered as red silk, is contradicted by the purchase record describing it as grey cotton (S2). Claim B, that lot K19 met its minimum wash-fastness rating on receipt, remains unresolved because no specific test results for lot K19 are provided; the vendor brochure (S3) only states that the product family generally meets the rating, without lot-specific confirmation. Given the lack of direct compliance evidence for lot K19, a customer representative cannot confidently confirm compliance at this time.","follow_up":{"S4":"independent laboratory report on a retained receipt sample places K19 at or above the specified wash-fastness minimum."}}

Claim C is decisively contradicted by the purchase record S2 describing the lot as grey cotton, not red silk. Initially, claim B was unresolved due to lack of specific test data, but the independent lab report S4 provides direct evidence that lot K19 meets the wash-fastness minimum, supporting claim B. Therefore, with compliance confirmed by S4, a customer representative can confirm compliance for lot K19."}

parsed.note: Claim A is decisively supported by the signed purchase record S1. Claim C is decisively contradicted by the purchase record S2 describing the lot as grey cotton, not red silk. Initially, claim B was unresolved due to lack of specific test data, but the independent lab report S4 provides direct evidence that lot K19 meets the wash-fastness minimum, supporting claim B. Therefore, with compliance confirmed by S4, a customer representative can confirm compliance for lot K19.
